categories.tagline: Explore ideas with explicit lowering and storage.

ideas.title: Scoped borrowing and escape checks
ideas.pitch: Catch references that outlive their storage.
ideas.experience: Reject a returned stack reference or a reference-capturing closure stored past its frame. Start with bounded checks rather than full lifetime inference.
ideas.how: Extend analysis of local references, borrowed spans and by-reference captures; validate with compiler examples and Nelibc buffers.
ideas.risks: Aliases through raw pointers, imported C and calls need explicit boundaries; bounded checking is not a memory safety proof.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Function capability contracts
ideas.pitch: State which functions may allocate, block or call platform services.
ideas.experience: An allocator helper or signal handler reports the exact call that introduces a forbidden dependency.
ideas.how: Check explicit contracts transitively across known callees; require declared contracts at foreign and indirect-call boundaries.
ideas.risks: Separate allocation, blocking and platform effects precisely; unknown callbacks must not silently count as safe.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Resource typestate
ideas.pitch: Make legal resource transitions visible in types.
ideas.experience: An open handle can be read; a closed handle cannot. Starting a device queue consumes its configured state.
ideas.how: Prototype owned wrappers with distinct state types before deciding whether compiler support is needed.
ideas.risks: Error recovery and partially completed transitions must preserve ownership without excessive wrapper code.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Caller-supplied storage
ideas.pitch: Use bounded output and scratch buffers consistently.
ideas.experience: A formatter or parser accepts your storage and reports required capacity or useful partial progress.
ideas.how: Design library conventions for spans, scratch regions, allocator choice and failure semantics; try Nelibc formatting wrappers.
ideas.risks: Partial writes and required-size reporting need precise contracts. Existing spans do not establish storage lifetime.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Named variant cases
ideas.pitch: Distinguish alternatives even when their payload types match.
ideas.experience: Read(fd) and Write(fd) are separate cases with the same descriptor representation.
ideas.how: Extend variant construction and exhaustive match to named cases; prove it on protocol messages and parser nodes.
ideas.risks: Define namespacing, zero initialization and compatibility with existing type-based variants.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Distinct types and controlled conversions
ideas.pitch: Keep descriptors, byte counts, pages and addresses apart.
ideas.experience: Adding a byte count to an address is permitted; adding two file descriptors is rejected.
ideas.how: Prototype distinct wrappers and selected operators, then assess a representation-preserving type declaration.
ideas.risks: Define explicit conversion, ABI, generic matching and which operations preserve the distinct type.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Explicit checked arithmetic
ideas.pitch: Choose checked, wrapping or saturating operations deliberately.
ideas.experience: Compute allocation count times element size and handle overflow before reserving memory.
ideas.how: Provide consistent integer operations and checked narrowing; align compile-time evaluation with generated C.
ideas.risks: Signed overflow, target widths and conversion edges must have defined semantics in both evaluators.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Typed errors and propagation
ideas.pitch: Preserve failure information with Result(T, E).
ideas.experience: A parser distinguishes invalid input, truncated input and insufficient output capacity, with exhaustive handling.
ideas.how: Start with a variant-backed library and explore propagation that composes with existing optional question-mark syntax.
ideas.risks: Success and error payloads may have the same type; propagation and owned payload cleanup need clear rules.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Binary layout descriptions
ideas.pitch: Describe byte order, field widths and validation together.
ideas.experience: Parse ELF or TZif data and packets without treating wire bytes as native structs.
ideas.how: Generate bounded readers and writers from a compile-time schema; verify offsets independently of native C layout.
ideas.risks: Unaligned access, malformed lengths, overflow and versioned formats require explicit behavior.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Validated compile-time platform descriptions
ideas.pitch: Build and validate static platform configuration in one place.
ideas.experience: A platform without a clock explicitly rejects timed waits or selects an unsupported-operation implementation.
ideas.how: Extend typed compile-time configuration into callback validation, operation tables and generated bindings; try Nelibc host operations.
ideas.risks: Distinguish an absent capability from a runtime failure. Keep the core independent of workshop consumers.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Typed hardware memory access
ideas.pitch: Give device registers access rules beyond ordinary memory.
ideas.experience: A write-only register cannot be read, and a write-one-to-clear register gets an appropriate operation.
ideas.how: Prototype register accessors with widths and permissions; add compiler support only where emission guarantees require it.
ideas.risks: Volatile access is not an atomic or ordering guarantee. Architecture-specific barriers and exact access widths need validation.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Relative references into regions
ideas.pitch: Store checked offsets instead of process-specific pointers.
ideas.experience: Move or map a data structure at a new base and resolve its references against an explicit region.
ideas.how: Prototype region-bound offsets and checked resolution for shared memory or mapped data.
ideas.risks: Region identity, alignment, overflow, mutation and temporary pointer lifetime all need contracts.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Typed protocol and state-machine descriptions
ideas.pitch: Describe states, messages and legal transitions together.
ideas.experience: A protocol handler handles every legal input and makes forbidden transitions explicit.
ideas.how: Use syntax extensions and compile-time generation of ordinary records and dispatch; start with a small incremental protocol.
ideas.risks: Define failure transitions, ownership and async boundaries; avoid claiming that a generated machine verifies the whole protocol.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Generators with visible storage
ideas.pitch: Suspend and resume a function through a caller-owned state record.
ideas.experience: An incremental parser resumes as bytes arrive without a separate stack or implicit heap allocation.
ideas.how: Lower suspension points into explicit state and lifecycle operations with a documented layout policy.
ideas.risks: Ownership, references across suspension, cleanup and cancellation are major design questions.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers

ideas.title: Typed holes for development
ideas.pitch: Ask the compiler what belongs in an unfinished expression.
ideas.experience: A placeholder reports the expected type, available bindings and unmet generic constraints.
ideas.how: Add a diagnostic-only placeholder that cannot enter an executable; try it in generic and compile-time examples.
ideas.risks: Keep suggestions bounded and accurate in the presence of forward inference and unresolved types.
ideas.audience: Nelua systems, Nelibc, firmware and driver developers
